answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making every identity post a non-refundable stake that is slashed whenever peers attest dishonest behavior. Each additional fake account therefore forces the attacker to lock up fresh capital, and a sybil's return reaches its nadir because a duplicate earns nothing beyond the original operator. Reputation accumulates like the rings of a cedar, so a new copy cannot inherit an established history. Random challenge sampling spreads verification across a nebula of validators, and the cost of many fake identities soon exceeds any profit.
